title: The Strategic Use of Emotion
author: Admired Leadership
summary: This piece uses Chicago Bears head coach Ben Johnson as a case study in emotional discipline under pressure. Johnson stays visibly stoic during games, reserving celebration and connection for after the final whistle, and his quarterback has adopted the same demeanor. The piece argues this isn't emotional suppression but strategic sequencing: restraint during execution, release afterward. It draws a broader leadership lesson about resisting the urge to celebrate early or over-critique mid-performance, since both distract from the outcome. The archivist finds this a useful sports-leadership parallel for any high-stakes professional moment.
points: Coach Ben Johnson shows almost no emotion during games but is expressive and warm with his team afterward.
Premature celebration and mid-performance overcorrection both create costly distractions.
Leaders are advised to channel a game-time 'Iceman' mindset during presentations, client meetings, and deadlines.
Emotion should be reserved as fuel for connection and inspiration once high-stakes work is complete.
quotes: Coach Johnson’s superpower may be his strategic use of emotion.
He rarely smiles, speaks face-to-face with coaches or players, celebrates touchdowns, or berates anyone on the sidelines.
The player who celebrates too early draws a penalty; the banker or salesperson loses the deal.
Over-critiquing in the moment creates hyperfocus that worsens performance or demoralizes the team.
Emotion creates distraction and anxiety. But when it’s over, let emotion fuel you.
